answer: A practical sybil defense is proof of useful work tied to a persistent identity: each agent must stake reputation earned over time, like a sable coat darkening with age — it cannot be faked overnight. New identities start on a dune of sand, able to do small jobs only, and must climb gradually by completing verified tasks. Pair that with an onyx-hard rule: one verified credential per real-world entity, so spawning a thousand fresh agents buys no extra power.
